label: early original-phase l/r/n/i/g/x after a prefix of u/p/q/k/b/3/v/a/m
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (98% of mass): it fires at t=1-4, peaking at t=2-3, and never at t=0. The input is usually one of l, r, n, i, g, x (l is strongest, at 8.5x lift), with s weaker. It fires most when the sequence starts with, and is mostly made of, tokens from u/p/q/k/b/3/v/a/m. The top activations look like k u a [l] and u p a [l]: a prefix of u/k/p, then a, then l. It is mostly silent on the delimiter and the copy phase (about 2% of mass, small weak activations at the first output steps). It is weak at t>=5, on repeated occurrences of a token, and when the prefix contains other letters. Magnitude rises with how well the prefix matches the u/p/q/k/a set and with the input being l. It looks like a graded, distributed combination of token identity and prefix contents, so the boolean predicate misses about a third of the mass and has many false positives (dev F1 0.54).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & prev_tok=a (+8.05), t=1 & prev_tok=g (+6.27), t=1 & prev_tok=r (+5.58), t=1 & in_tok=l (+5.43), t=3 (+4.71), in_tok=g (+4.26). Lower it: prev_tok=z (-2.97), recall_idx=4 (-2.70), in_tok=p (-2.43), in_tok=k (-2.20).
